I will still plant maize on all 1.7 mu this year. On my small piece of land, I do not dare cut fertilizer too hard, because if the ears come out small, that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. Last year I would have put the main fertilizer down before sowing and then chased one more time around the big flare stage, and I will do about the same this year. Around here, if a hybrid did well in other people’s fields, I will follow that, so I will use hybrid maize seed, not old saved seed. My land has well irrigation, so I can hold the crop steady if it turns dry. I will give enough base fertilizer, then one topdressing when the maize is growing fast. Phosphorus and potassium I will mainly put in the base, nitrogen I will split. For 1 mu, I will count about 20 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium. Water I will probably give 3 times if the rain is not enough: once after sowing if the ground is dry, once around jointing, once around tasseling and grain filling. Pesticide I will not spray blindly, but I usually end up using it about 2 times, one for weeds early and one for insects or disease later if pressure comes. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because the area is small and that is the easiest for me. If weather is normal, I will look for about 550 kg per mu.
